- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.1) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment is positive (avg > 0.1) and model forecast is below recent 10-day average, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; apply a +0.5–1.0% bias to early forecast points.
- When sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.2 → -0.1 → +0.2), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment to forecast adjustment.
- If model forecast is >1.5% above recent 10-day average and sentiment is neutral, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by >2% in 3 consecutive days, apply a “mean reversion” correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
